full_judgment:
Md. Mozammel Hoque, J: This Rule was issued directing the State, represented by the Deputy Commissioner, Dhaka and the District Magistrate, Dhaka, to show cause as to the Order No.23 dated 5.4.95: passed by the learned Additional Sessions. Judge, 2nd Court, Dhaka, in Sessions Case No. 137 of 1994, appointing one Mr. Asaduzzaman, Assistant Public Prosecutor, as State defence lawyer for absconding accused Akhtaruzzaman Babu, passed in pursuance of an order under. Memo No. 647/Bi/sha:8/93/94 dated 4.4.95 superseding the earlier letter of appointment of Mr. Serajul Huq, the Senior Advocate of Bangladesh Supreme Court, appointed for the aforesaid absconding accused Akhtaruzzaman Babu on the prayer of the present petitioner should not be set aside. 

 2. Facts of the case, in short, are that a case, namely, Sessions Trial Case No. 137 of 1994 is pending in the Court of the learned Additional Sessions Judge, 2nd Court, Dhaka, against seven persons, including Mr, Akhtaruzzaman Chowdhury alias Babu. This Mr. Akhtaruzzaman Chowdhury alias Babu appeared before the Court and after getting bail he is absconding. It is a case under Section 302/34 of the Penal Code and charge sheet was also submitted against the. seven persons under Sections 302/109/34 of the Penal Code. It appears from application that the one Assistant Public Prosecutor Mr. Anowar Zahed Bhuiyan was first appointed as State defence lawyer for absconding accused Akhtaruzzaman Babu by an order No. 6 dated 3.7.94. 

 3. The present petitioner being the wife of the absconding accused Akhtaruzzaman Babu filed an application before the Hon'ble Minister, Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs, for appointing a senior experienced lawyer as state defence lawyer to defend her husband in the instant murder case. On such application the Ministry of Law. Justice and Parliamentary Affairs issued an order on 27.10.94 directing the Deputy Commissioner. Dhaka, to arrange for appointment of an experienced lawyer to defend Mr. Akhtaruzzaman Babu in the above murder case. This order of the Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs is annexed as Annexuie A to this application. From the two orders one dated 8.11.94, Annexure-A(1) and another dated 19.11.94, Annexure-A(2) issued by the District Magistrate and Additional District Magistrate, Dhaka, respectively, it appears that when the order of the Ministry reached the office of the District Magistrate, the present petitioner, being the wife of the absconding accused, filed an application on 31.10.94 praying for appointment of Mr. Serajul Huq the Senior Advocate of he Supreme Court of Bangladesh to defend her husband. In pursuance of the order of the Ministry as well as the application of the order of the present petitioner the District Magistrate, Dhaka, appointed Mr. Serajul Huq, the Senior Advocate of the Supreme Court, as a State defence lawyer to defend the absconding accused Akhtaruzzaman Babu. 

 4. In pursuance of the orders of the District Magistrate as stated above the learned Additional Sessions Judge, Dhaka, by order dated 10.11.94 appointed Mr. Serajul Huq Advocate as state defence lawyer for Akhtaruzzaman Babu. Since then Mr. Serajul Huq Advocate appeared before the Court on behalf of the absconding accused Mr. Akhtaruzzaman Babu on 12.11.94, 7.1.95, 8.1.95; 21.1.95, 4.2.95, 5.2.95; 25.2.95, 18.3.95, 19.3.95 and 1.4.95 and conducted the case on his behalf by making cross-examination to the P.Ws. While Mr. Serajul Huq Advocate has beep conducting the case on be half of the absconding accused Akhtaruzzaman Babu, by an order dated 5.4.95 the learned Additional Sessions Judge, 2nd Court, Dhaka, appointed Assistant Public Prosecutor Mr. Asaduzzaman as state defence lawyer for Akhtaruzzaman Babu on the basis of .a letter of the District Magistrate dated 4.4.95 which was sent to the Court for appointment of Assistant Public Prosecutor. Mr. Asaduzzaman as State defence lawyer for Akhtaruzzaman Babu and the order dated 8 by which Mr. Serajul Huq Advocale was appointed as State defence lawyer for Mr. Akhtaruzzaman Babu was withdrawn and rescinded. Being aggrieved by this order dated 5.4.95 the present petitioner preferred this revisional application and obtained the present Rule. 

 5. In the instant case the facts a not disputed at all. It appears from the record that alter appointment of Mr. Serajul Huq Advocate to defend the case of tile absconding accused Akhtaruzzaman Babu, he attended the Court on 10 (ten) occasions and conducted the case on behalf of his absconding client by doing cross-examination to the P.Ws. After examination of three P.Ws. all on a sudden this order of the District Magistrate was passed on 4.4.95 cancelling the appointment of Mr. Serajul Huq Advocate and on his place the District Magistrate appointed another Assistant Public Prosecutor Mr. Asaduzzaman to appear and conduct the case on behalf of the absconding accused. Mr. Amirul Islam, the learned Advocate appearing for the present petitioner, submits that this cancellation of appointment of Mr. Serajul Huq Advocate as defence lawyer was passed in complete violation of the provision of Section 340 of the Code of Criminal Procedure and Article 31 and 33 of the Constitution, He further submits that this order of cancellation of appointment of Mr. Serajul Hug was passed hastily without showing any reason whatsoever. He further submits that this action of cancellation of appointment of Mr. Serajul Huq was done behind the back of the pre-petitioner and as such it is a malafide action of the authority. Since the appointment of Mr. Serajul Huq Advocate was cancelled, it will affect and prejudice the fair trial in the instant case in view of the fact that the cancellation of appointment of Mr. Serajul Huq and appointment of another Assistant Public Prosecutor will seriously prejudice the interest of the accused and Create an impression in his mind that he will not get fair trial and justice in the case. 

 7. Mr. Amir-ul Islam submits that since Mr. Serajul Huq was appointed by the District Magistrate on the direction of the Government to defend the case of the absconding accused and he appeared on ten occasions and conducted the case on behalf of the absconding accused, the sudden cancellation of his appointment will seriously prejudice the fair trial of the accused He has drawn our attention to Section 340 of the Code of Criminal Procedure which provides that any person accused of an offence before a criminal Court or against whom proceedings are instituted under this Code in any such Court, may of right to be defended by a pleader, since the offence in the present case is punishable with death, either the State or the Court will appoint a lawyer to defend him and this is along standing established principle of this country. Accordingly, in the instant case though Mr. Akhtaruzzaman Babu was absconding, yet Assistant Public Prosecutor Mr. Anowar Zaher Bhuiyan was rust appointed as State defence lawyer for the absconding accused by the State on 3.7.94. So it appears that the state appointed a lawyer to defend the absconding in the instant case. 

 8. Then the wife of the absconding accused filed an application before the Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs for appoint in of an experienced lawyer to defend her husband and on the basis of an application the Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs by an order dated 28.10.94, directed the Deputy Commissioner, Dhaka, for appointment of an experienced lawyer to defend Mr. Akhtaruzzaman Babu in the instant case. While this order reached the District Magistrate, Dhaka, the present petitioner filed another application before the District Magistrate, Dhaka, suggesting that Senior Advocate Mr. Serajul Huq may be appointed to defend her husband and on such application as well as on the direction of the Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs, the District Magistrate, Dhaka, ultimately appointed Mr. Serajul Huq Advocate by an order dated 8.11.94. This appointment was sent to Mr. Serajul Huq Advocate for his consent who accepted the appointment on the terms and conditions given by the District Magistrate in the letter of appointment. While he was conducting the case on behalf of the absconding accused, all on a sudden his appointment was cancelled by the order of the District Magistrate, Dhaka, dated 4.4.95. 

 10. In support of his contention that the absconding accused will not get fair trial and he will be prejudiced by the cancellation of appointment of Mr. Serajul Huq, Mr. Islam has referred to the cases of State of Madhya Prodesh Shoma Ram and others, A.I.R. 1966 (S.C.), 1910 and Emperor Vs. Sukhdev and others. AIR.1929 (Lah.), 705. M Islam has also referred to another case of lshtikhar Uddin Vs. Corwn, 6 DLR (WP)127. This 6 DLR case Section 340 of the Code of Criminal Procedure came up for .consideration of their lordships. In disposing of that case their lordships observed that the only effect of Section 340(1) is that once State lawyer has been engaged either by the accused himself or on his behalf, no Court can deny such state lawyer the right of Mr. Islam further submits that since In Criminal Procedure Code provision was made for trial of the absconding accused, by way of amendment of law, the State is bound to appoint a laWyer to the choice of the accused. He further submits that right of appearance of a lawyer can not be taken away arbitrarily to the prejudide of the accused. 

 11. In the instant case it appears that on the application of the wife of absconding accused, Mr. Serajul Huq Advocate was appointed and he appeared in the Court and conducted the case on several occasions on behalf of the absconding accused. But all on a sudden his appointment was cancelled without showing any reason whatsoever. There is nothing in the record to show that Mr. Serajul Huq Advocate misconducted himself in conducting the case of the absconding accused nor a better and more experienced lawyer than Mr. Serajul Mg was appointed to conduct the case of Mr. Akhtaruzzaman Babu by cancelling the appointment of Mr. Serajul Huq. In this view o the matter, we find that there is every apprehension in the mind of the absconding accused that he will get fair trial in this case, although the state lawyer like Mr. Serajul Huq was appointed by the State on the application of his wife. 

 12. Let us now examine the submissions of the learned Deputy Attorney General. On behalf of the State no affidavit-in-opposition has been filed in this case. The learned Deputy Attorney General submits that Mr. Serajul Huq was appointed beyond the panel of Assistant Public Prosecutor and the District Magistrate has no locus-standi to appoint a lawyer as state defence lawyer outside the panel of A.P.P. But the learned Deputy Attorney General has failed to show any provision of law or rule or regulation as regards appointment of state defence lawyer. Rather the Manual of the Legal Remembrancer clearly shows that the District Magistrate is the actual authority to appoint a lawyer for the State. It is a long-standing established principle that the State is represented by the District Magistrate both in civil and criminal matters in the district. The submission of the learned Deputy Attorney General is contrary to the record of the Government in view of the fact that on the direction of the Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs, the District Magistrate, Dhaka, appointed Mr. Serajul Huq to defend the case of the absconding accused Akhtaruzzaman Bairn on the application of the present petitioner. So, the submission of the learned Deputy Attorney General is absolutely baseless. 

 14. Lastly, the learned Deputy Attorney General submits that since Mr. Akhtaruzzaman Babu is a fugitive from law, he is not entitled to get any relief from this Court. Mr. Akhtaruzzaman Babu as such is not coming for any relief from this Court. It is admitted position that he is absconding, and his wife on his behalf filed an application to the Ministry for appointment of an, experienced lawyer to defend her absconding husband. On such application the Government directed the District Magistrate to appoint an experienced lawyer and on another applications to the District Magistrate, the District Magistrate appointed Mr. Serajul Huq Advocate as State defence lawyer for Mr. Akhtaruzzaman Babu. So, this appointment of Mr. Serajul Huq Advocate was made by the District Magistrate on the application of the present petitioner who is the wife of the absconding accused. Since the appointment, which was made on the application, of the present petitioner, was cancelled, definitely the present petitioner is an aggrieved person and she can challenge the impugned order passed by the learned Additional Sessions Judge as well as the order of cancellation of appointment of Mr. Serajul Huq by the District Magistrate, Dhaka. In the instant case the present petitioner is praying for an order from this Court in a very limited manner inasmuch as she is praying that on her prayer the appointment of Mr. Serajul Huq was made as state defence lawyer. But without showing any reason by the State to her, the appointment of Mr. Serajul Huq was cancelled and an Assistant Public Prosecutor was appointed to defend her husband and as such she prays before this 'Court that there is apprehension in her mind that there can not be a fair trial in the instant case where her husband is an accused. 

 15. On the point of fugitive from law, the learned Deputy Attorney General has referred the case of Chand Shah Vs. Crown, 8 DLR(F.C.), 24 and the case Khalilur Rahman Vs. The State, 33 DLR 12. It is the Settled principle that a fugitive from justice so long as he remains beyond the 'reach of-the Court is not entitled to any relief. This is a long standing established principle and there is no dispute over But in the peculiar facts and circumstances. of the present case it appears to us that this principle that a fugitive not entitled to any relief is not applicable in the present case inasmuch as the present petitioner filed an application for appointment of Mr. Serajul Huq as State defence lawyer for her husband and the appointment of Mr. Serajul Huq was cancelled without showing my reasons to her. In the case of State Vs Emdad A Bepari, 36 DLR, 333, it is held by the Court that conviction of a person charged with committing an offence punishable with death, without he being represented by a lawyer is illegal. In such a case a lawyer has to be appointed to defend the accused. Since the offence is punishable with death in the instant case, even if he is a fugitive, the State first appointed a defence lawyer which was ultimately changed by the State on the application of the present petitioner. So, we do not find any substance in the above contention of the learned Deputy Attorney General. Rather, we find that if Mr. Serajul Huq Advocate conducts the case of the absconding accused as State defence lawyer, the State will not be prejudiced in any manner, rather the Court will be benefited with the able assistance of a Senior Advocate like Mr. Serajul Huq. 

 16. Considering the provisions of law as enunciated in Section 340 of the Code of criminal Procedure and right of a citizen under Article 31 and 32 of the Constitution and also relying upon the aforesaid decisions as referred to by Mr. Amirul Islam, particularly, the 6 DLR case, we are of the view that, for ends of justice and fair trial the impugned order passed by the learned Additional Sessions Judge, 2nd Court, Dhaka, cannot be Sustained in law. We hold that the action of cancellation of appointment of Mr. Serajul of as State defence lawyer and the impugned order of the learned Additional Sessions Judge, 2nd Court, Dhaka, will prejudice the fair trial and there every apprehension that the absconding accused will not get justice and fair trial in view of the fact that the hasty action of change of defence lawyer was made with some. ulterior motive and as such the impugned order cannot be sustained in law. 

 17. In the result, this Rule is made absolute and the impugned order dated 5.4.95 passed by the learned Additional. Sessions Judge, 2nd Court Dhaka, is hereby set aside and the appointment of Mr. Asaduzzaman, Assistant Public Prosecutor, in the instant case a, state defence, lawyer of Mr. Akhtaruzzaman Babu by the order dated.4.4.95 is hereby cancelled. The learned Advocate Mr. Serajul Huq, shall appear and conduct the aforesaid Sessions Case for and on behalf of the absconding accused Mr. Akhtaruzzaman Babu till the termination of the proceeding, if anything otherwise does not take place in the meantime. The order of stay passed by this Court is hereby vacated and the learned Judge of the trial Court is directed to proceed with the Sessions Case in-accordance 'with law. Let an advance order be issued immediately.
